the role of Apolipoprotein-E (ApoE) in the progression of Alzheimer’s disease (Disease) and aims to identify the underlying molecular and cellular mechanisms.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ApoE iso-form specific effects are not only relevant in astrocytes and neurons, but that ApoE also has a significant influence on microglia physiology.
ApoE iso-form specific effects on microgliosis are complex and may be dependent on disease context.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ApoE2 and ApoE3 are both able to increase phagocytotic capacity in microglia in vitro and that ApoE3 and ApoE4 are both able to promote microglia migration.
ApoE is upregulated in microglia in AD and that ApoE isoforming microglia might have different functional effects on microglial physiology in AD.
ApoE isotypes have differential effects on microglial physiology and that ApoE3 and ApoE2 are more effective than Apo4 in microglial phagocytotic behavior in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ApoE4 isoform is not only associated with increased risk to develop Alzheimer’s disease, but may also be involved in the progression of disease by affecting microglia function.
ApoE isotypes may not only affect Aβ clearance but also the clearance of other pathogenic proteins.
ApoE isoforming microglia may be a novel therapeutic target in AD.
